name: Tromsø Airport
before:
The fifth busiest airport in Norway, on the western shore of Tromsoya island. It is the hub for Wideroe's regional network into Finnmark, so anything heading further north connects through here.

The runway is 2,447 metres and the airport is owned and run by Avinor, the state operator. It handled a little over 1.9 million passengers and more than 43,000 aircraft movements in 2014.

There are two terminals. Terminal B dates from 1977 and Terminal A opened in 1997, alongside a runway extension and a new control tower.

The airport opened in September 1964, replacing a water aerodrome at Skattora which had served Tromso until then. Lufttransport has its main operating base here, and Norwegian has flown from the airport since 1992.
after:
The fifth busiest airport in Norway, at Langnes a few kilometres from the centre of Tromsø. It is the main hub for flights between southern Norway and Finnmark, so a lot of journeys further north connect through here.

The runway is about 2,450 metres, and the airport is owned and run by Avinor, the state operator. It handled about 2.9 million passengers in 2025.

The airport opened in September 1964, replacing the seaplane base at Skattøra.
